title: Persecution of minorities
log: 2026-11-01T08:04:35Z match: Claude Haiku 5.5 found no bank point the same, so it is written new

match.reason: The bank's Holocaust point centres on genocide, mass murder and the camps, which goes well beyond the new point's focus on the stripping of rights and persecution of minorities, including Sinti and Roma, so it is a related but different idea rather than a match.

draft.title: Persecution of minorities
card: The Nazi regime in Germany blamed Jews for the country's problems. This idea was spread by propaganda and hatred long before the war.
Nuremberg Laws
passed in 1935. They took away German citizenship from Jews and banned marriage between Jews and non-Jews.
Violence
Persecution grew from lost rights to attacks. On Kristallnacht in November 1938, Jewish shops, homes and synagogues were attacked across Germany.
Holocaust
During the Second World War the Nazis murdered about six million Jews. Sinti and Roma people were also persecuted and many were murdered.
draft.remember: Persecution of Jews in Nazi Germany moved from loss of rights to violence and, in the war, mass murder.

a.q: What did the Nuremberg Laws of 1935 do?
opts: Took away the citizenship of Jews in Germany
Ordered the murder of Jews across Europe
Forced Jews to leave Germany within a year
Closed all Jewish shops in Germany in one night
a.why: The laws removed citizenship and banned marriage between Jews and non-Jews. They did not order mass murder, which came later in the war. Mass murder is the tempting answer, but the laws were about removing rights.
a.clue: The laws took away status, not lives.

b.q: A historian says the Holocaust did not come from nowhere. Which fact from the card best supports this view?
opts: Rights were removed in 1935 and violence grew before the war
Sinti and Roma people were also persecuted in Germany
About six million Jews were murdered during the war
Kristallnacht took place across Germany in 1938
b.why: Loss of rights in 1935, then violence in 1938, shows persecution built up in steps before the war. The number murdered shows the scale, not the build up. Kristallnacht alone is one step, not the whole pattern.
b.clue: Look for the answer that shows a sequence of steps.

a.best: Took away the citizenship of Jews in Germany

b.best: Rights were removed in 1935 and violence grew before the war
also_right: Kristallnacht took place across Germany in 1938

problems.detail: The intended option stands out. It is the longest, the only one with two linked steps, and it echoes the card's 'Persecution grew from lost rights to attacks' and the remember line. The clue 'shows a sequence of steps' then points straight at it, so a student can pick it without weighing the evidence.

Kristallnacht in 1938 was violence before the war, so it also supports the view that the Holocaust 'did not come from nowhere'. Only the word 'best' separates it from the intended answer, which may confuse students who pick it for a sound reason.

check.summary: The facts are accurate and question a is sound. In question b the right option is the longest and is signposted by the clue, and the Kristallnacht option is also defensible as supporting evidence.

proposal.title: Persecution of minorities
card: The Nazi regime in Germany blamed Jews for the country's problems. This idea was spread by propaganda and hatred long before the war.

Violence
Persecution grew from lost rights to attacks. On Kristallnacht in November 1938, Jewish shops, homes and synagogues were attacked across Germany.
Holocaust

Forced Jews to leave Germany within a year
Closed all Jewish shops in Germany in one night
a.why: The laws removed citizenship and banned marriage between Jews and non-Jews. They did not order mass murder, which came later in the war. Mass murder is the tempting answer, but the laws were about removing rights.

b.q: Lena is making a timeline of Nazi persecution of Jews for a class display. Which order of events is correct?
opts: Nuremberg Laws, then Kristallnacht, then the Holocaust
Kristallnacht, then Nuremberg Laws, then the Holocaust
Nuremberg Laws, then the Holocaust, then Kristallnacht
The Holocaust, then Nuremberg Laws, then Kristallnacht
b.why: The Nuremberg Laws came in 1935, Kristallnacht in November 1938, and the Holocaust during the war from 1939 to 1945. Putting Kristallnacht first is tempting because it was so well known, but rights were removed three years before it.
b.clue: Check the year or period given for each event.
